newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Lonrho S.Africa lockout strike ends - union.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho S.Africa lockout strike ends - union.

text.p: A lockout dispute between Lonrho Plc's Western North Platinum mine management in South Africa and the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) had been resolved, the union said on Friday.
"The Western North Platinum mine lockout was resolved yesterday evening (April 24) at a meeting between the union and management," the NUM said in a statement.
On Thursday night workers went underground for the first time since the lockout began on April 18.

Mine management locked out 9,000 mineworkers following a two-hour sit-in to protest against the appointment of a new underground manager, who workers claimed had changed workplace regulations without consulting the union.
The NUM said it had called off a court interdict that it had applied for.

"However, we still have to resolve some matters...including the payment of days lost during the lockout and also to determine whether the lockout was lawful or not," NUM Rustenburg regional co-ordinator Mahlakeng Mahlakeng said.
